To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the enterohepatiic circulation of bile salts is a critical regulator of cholesterol homeostatis and that bile salts are ligands for nuclear receptors.
bile salts and oxysterol cholesterol metabolites are ligands for the nuclear hormone receptors LXR and FXRs, respectively, that act to coordinate cholesterol and bile acid metabolism.
nuclear hormone receptors LXR and FXr act in a coordinated fashion to control the enterohepatocytic circulation of bile salts to prevent cholesterol and bile salt accumulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of bile salts and other nuclear hormone receptors as ligand sensors for cholesterol metabolism and bile salt homeostasis.

the molecular mechanisms by which the bile acid sensor, FXR, and the bile salt transporter, NTCP, are coordinately regulated by bile acids and the role of FXR in the regulation of bile salt transport and metabolism.
the role of bile acids as ligands for bile acid nuclear receptors and the effect on cholesterol homeostasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nuclear hormone receptor system is a major regulatory mechanism for cholesterol homeostasis.
the enterohepatobiliary system, which is composed of liver and intestine, is the major organ responsible for the regulation of cholesterol balance.
bile salts are not simply a byproduct of cholesterol metabolism, but rather, bile salts and nuclear hormones receptors are essential for maintaining cholesterol homeostasis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bile acids are the ligand for FXR, which is a nuclear hormone receptor.
nuclear hormone receptor agonists and antagonists may be developed to positively affect cholesterol and bile salt metabolism.
the nuclear hormone receptors LXR and FXr, in conjunction with retinoid X receptors, function as bile acid and oxysterol sensors to coordinate cholesterol and bile acid metabolism.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the enterohepanctic circulation of bile acids, and the coordinated action of FXR, LXR and their obligate partner retinoid X receptors, are critical to the regulation of cholesterol metabolism and bile acid homeoestasis, and that bile acid metabolism is an important component of cholesterol metabolism.

the coordinated transcription factor activity of nuclear hormone receptors LXR and FXRs, each dimerizing to retinoid x receptors, is the key to the regulation of cholesterol metabolism in the liver and peripheral tissues and bile salt metabolism in the intestine and liver.
the enterohepidatic circulation of bile acids, which is regulated by FXR in the liver, is a critical determinant of cholesterol homeostatis.
